To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FdTSPO is a tetrapyrrole binding protein that is involved in stress response in the cyanobacterial model organism Fremyella diplophion.

F. diplosipon has 3 homologs of TSPO proteins, that all 3 are capable of binding heme and/or biliverdin, that all 4 proteins are differentially regulated by different abiotic stressors, and that FdTSPO is required for the regulation of the expression of genes involved in tetrapyrrole metabolism.

the cyanobacteriun Fremyella dipolsiphon possesses three genes that encode homologs of tryptophan rich sensory proteins (TSPO) that are differentially expressed in response to light, osmotic, salt, and nutrient stresses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the roles of TSPO homologs in the regulation of tetrapyrrole metabolism and function.
understanding the roles of F. diplosipho n TSPO proteins in tetrapyrrole metabolism and homeostasis, and in the stress response.
the identification and characterization of novel proteins that regulate the cellular response to environmental stress in the cyanobacterial model F. diplosphon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FdTSPOs have distinct roles in F. dipolsiphon, but that the specific roles remain unclear.
TSPO proteins are likely involved in stress and/or nutrient responses in F. diplosiphon.
the three F. diplosipon TSPO proteins appear, at least in part, to be involved in tetrapyrrole-mediated responses to environmental stresses in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
F. diplosipon has evolved a complex regulatory network of 3 TSPO proteins that function to sense and regulate tetrapyrroles in response to multiple abiotic stresses.
TSPOs are involved in the regulation of multiple tetrapyrrole-dependent cellular functions in cyanobacteria.

F. diplosphon possesses 3 TSPO genes that are differentially regulated by light-, nutrient-, and stress-dependent signals and are likely to have distinct roles in tetrapyrrole-mediated stress responses in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TSPO homologs in cyanobacteria are likely to have distinct, but overlapping, roles in the regulation of cellular responses to environmental stress.
F. diplosphion possesses 3 distinct TSPO homologs, which have overlapping functions in vivo, and are differentially regulated by different environmental stresses.
the 3 TSPO homologs in F. diplospohon are differentially regulated in response to distinct abiotic stresses.
